answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small bond locked for a full epoch, so spinning up thousands of fake identities gets expensive fast. Picture a terrace: trust is earned level by level, never granted all at once. A prism of independent checks — proof of work, peer attestation, and on-chain history — refracts every claim, so one forged credential alone cannot pass. And a thread of continuous activity ties reputation to past behavior, making throwaway identities worthless while honest agents compound trust.
